## Findings
- claim-1: Conditional on task 85’s interval presentation and complete \(h_1\)-row hypothesis, for \(0\le k\le b=\min(i,j)\), \[ M_{d+k}/L_k\cong\mathbb Z,\qquad [C_x]=(-1)^x[C_0]\quad(0\le x\le k), \] where \(C_x=P_{x,k-x}\). The isomorphism sends \([C_0]\) to \(1\).
- claim-2: Put \[ X_k=P_{k,0}=s_{((i+1)^k,i^{j-k})},\qquad Y_k=P_{0,k}=s_{(i^j,k)}. \] Then degreewise \[ [X_k]=(-1)^k[Y_k],\qquad [Y_k]=(-1)^k[X_k]. \] Thus the change-of-basis matrix from the horizontal endpoint basis \(([X_k])\) to the vertical endpoint basis \(([Y_k])\) is the \(1\times1\) matrix \(\bigl((-1)^k\bigr)\), for every \(0\le k\le b\).
- claim-3: The requested truncated conditional target is established; no globalization claim is made.
## Strategy
Use task 85’s presentation \(M_{d+k}=\bigoplus_{x=0}^k\mathbb ZC_x\) and relations \(L_k=\sum_{x=0}^{k-1}\mathbb Z(C_x+C_{x+1})\). These imply \([C_x]=(-1)^x[C_0]\); the homomorphism \(C_x\mapsto(-1)^x\) proves the cyclic quotient has no torsion. Identify \(Y_k=C_0\) and \(X_k=C_k\), yielding the scalar endpoint change of basis \((-1)^k\).

## Gaps
All conclusions are conditional on task 85’s invoked interval presentation and complete \(h_1\)-row hypothesis. No source grounding of those hypotheses is supplied here. No claim beyond degrees \(d,\ldots,d+b\) is made.

## Next
The requested truncated conditional target is established. Any globalization requires separate evidence.
